catalogue_requests.reason: The catalogue has no class for disabling a power-supply output as a safe-state action. The action takes no input, so it cannot be a refinement of cap.device.configure.v1; it is the safe_state=True action SAFE-045 needs at R2 and it writes the clone's all-channel OUTP OFF command.
catalogue_requests.summary: Disable all channel outputs of the power supply

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked; no hardware was used). The driver is a ScpiDriver over the SCPI command forms in 2230G.py, not over the upstream class: the constructor opens self.instr_address although its parameter is inst_address (2230G.py:37), and get_model is compared as a bound method so its model branches never run (2230G.py:568). The unit can be a 30-3, 30-6 or 60-3 (2230G.py:84), so every voltage and current setpoint uses Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json is a narrow example, not a device fact. The driver composes INST:NSEL n with VOLT, CURR or CHAN:OUTP on one SCPI line; the clone writes the selection and the setting as separate commands, so this exact composition is not shown in the clone and was not tried on an instrument. The e-stop and the safe-state action write OUTP OFF (2230G.py:820); this is a software output-off through the instrument's own command path, not an external hardware e-stop. The fake is a stateful analytic transport, not a recording or transcript: its identity string, start values, measured values and 10-ohm load are placeholders, not device facts. The hardware backend was never opened; pyvisa is only needed if the deployment chooses a VISA resource. The upstream package is not imported and its code was not run. Model-authored and unreviewed (reviewed_by is null); at R2 the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs a review. Not covered: a hardware run, the actual identity reply, the installed model, the unit's real voltage and current bounds, the semicolon composition on the instrument, and the instrument's response to a malformed or timed-out e-stop command. The gate digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
